title: Pick up and roll a die
instruction: Pick up the small blue cube and roll it like a die on the table. Release it so it tumbles freely, then leave it untouched until it stops.
context: Handling small game pieces and initiating a free roll are components of assisting someone with tabletop games. This task tests the physical manipulation; it does not test numerical face recognition, randomness or statistical fairness.
setup: Two YAM arms in the calibrated station scene; oak-coloured horizontal tabletop 1.10 m by 1.30 m, surface z=0.7475 m, centred at x=0.36 m and y=0 m. One blue, homogeneous 16 x 16 x 16 mm cube, specified mass 5 g, represents a plastic die without pips. Its centre starts at (0.20, 0.16, 0.7555) m with identity orientation. World x points away from the arm bases, y left, z up. Object jitter is zero. No other loose objects or rolling aids are present.
scoring: Version roll-a-die-v2. 0.25 for holding the die with its bottom at least 30 mm above the tabletop for 0.20 s, speed <=0.15 m/s, with a measured closed gripper less than 35 mm away. Release requires each gripper to be at least 70 mm away or to provide at least 2 mm geometric jaw clearance around the oriented cube; at least 22 mm nearest-TCP clearance, at least 12 mm bottom clearance, and a measured near-gravity acceleration interval. The reference orientation is the first pose of the uninterrupted verified free-flight history, or the confirmed release pose when no earlier interval qualifies. 0.5 requires a maximum tilt excursion of at least 90 degrees from that reference, measured as separation of world vertical expressed in the die frame. Pure world-vertical spin and accumulated small rocking do not count. A full revolution can qualify even if the final orientation returns to the reference. 1.0 requires the turnover followed by 1 continuous second resting on a face on the tabletop, speed <0.01 m/s, spin <0.25 rad/s, tilt <=10 degrees and both TCPs >=60 mm away. Leaving the permitted tabletop bounds or renewed gripper proximity after release invalidates all credit. Cumulative angular travel is diagnostic only. Exact predicates and replay algorithm are in scoring.py; the reviewer audit is in JUDGING.md.
run_limit: 1,200 control steps (60 seconds at 20 Hz), one episode per run.
reset_notes: Restore the cube to its specified pose and both arms to the station ready pose. run.py creates a fresh temporal scorer after every reset. Use a new log directory for each run.
fidelity: A sharp-edged, homogeneous blank cube approximates a plastic die; no engraved pips, rounded corners, numbered result, or statistical randomness is modeled. The initial implementation uses the adapter's primitive collision/friction defaults, which have not been calibrated to a physical die. Measured gripper clearance is a release/contact proxy, not a force-sensor contact measurement. Motion and scoring are audited at 20 Hz and may miss faster substep motion. These limits are documented for review.
scores: Scorer roll-a-die-v2, offline rescoring of retained measured simulation trajectories (not new physics runs). Dream-1 (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta): 0.0 after 1,200 control steps (60.00 simulated seconds), 25 requests in one continuous session with no retries. Scripted demonstration: 1.0 after 186 control steps (9.30 simulated seconds), maximum tilt excursion 133.207 degrees from the verified free-flight reference, cumulative motion 164.434 degrees, and 1.00 s continuous rest. Seed 0; fixed layout; same scorer and action limits. VALIDATION.json records evidence hashes; fresh repeat trials are pending GPU capacity.
